newsitem.title: USA: Albert says he is innocent of sex assault charges.
newsitem.headline: Albert says he is innocent of sex assault charges.

text.p: Sportscaster Marv Albert, appearing in public for the first time since he was charged with sexually assaulting a Virginia woman, on Thursday said he was innocent and that he would continue broadcasting.

"I would like to reassert my innocence and reiterate that all the charges against me are false and will be proven false in a court of law," a subdued Albert told a news conference at a Manhattan hotel. "I will continue my work with the NBA, NBC Sports and MSG network while I establish my innocence in a public courtroom."

The 53-year-old Albert was charged on Monday in Arlington Circuit Court with one felony count of forcible sodomy and one misdemeanor count of assault and battery after the alleged incident in an Arlington, Va., hotel room on Feb. 12.
Albert and his attorneys told reporters that he had not been interviewed by police, prosecutors or the grand jury that indicted him.

One of the most recognisable voices in American sports broadcasting with his trademark "Yesss!", Albert will call Saturday's third game of the Eastern Conference Finals between the Chicago Bulls and Miami Heat for NBC, the network said in a statement.
Albert and his lawyers declined to answer questions at the news conference. Several reporters shouted out questions that were ignored. One was heard to yell, "is biting a form of foreplay?"

Police said Albert allegedly became enraged with the 41-year-old woman, threw her on the bed, bit her violently on the back 15 times and forced her to perform oral sex. New York newspapers quoted police sources as saying the woman had refused Albert's request to join him for sex with another man.
Forcible sodomy carries a penalty of five years to life in prison and assault and battery is punishable by up to 12 months and a $2,500 fine.
WRC-TV in Washington reported on Wednesday that Albert's accuser faced a criminal charge for allegedly threatening to kill her former boyfriend.

Court documents showed the woman had pleaded not guilty to the misdemeanor charge, according to the report. The alleged threats were made in three cellular telephone calls placed to the boyfriend on March 13, WRC-TV reported.

Albert also broadcasts for the Madison Square Garden Network in New York, where he is famous as the decades-long commentator for the New York Knicks of the National Basketball Association and the New York Rangers of the National Hockey League.
